language.sample_text: ប្រយ័ត្ន — ការងារជួសជុលផ្លូវ
language.script_notes: Khmer script features distinctive right-pointing hooks and curls, distinguishing it from Thai script (which has an abundance of circles) and Lao script. Administrative terms like 'Sangkat' and 'Phum' appear in place names.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Red-and-white — most commonly a stone bollard with a red top and white base (often with a reflector in the red part), or striped red-and-white; the red pyramid-shaped top is a distinctive Cambodia tell.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Stone posts with a rounded or pyramidal red top.
road_furniture.curb_style: Minimal outside towns; wide dusty shoulders and open roadside space.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Cambodian road markers are stone with a white base and rounded red top, showing the road number on the narrow side and a town name plus distance on the main face. Chevron curve signs are black with yellow arrows — the reverse of the yellow-with-black-arrows convention used elsewhere in Southeast Asia.

architecture.roof_style: Sloped roofs on traditional stilt houses; ornate multi-tiered roofs on Buddhist temple (wat) buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal widespread on modern houses; tile on temples; thatch/palm on more traditional rural homes.
architecture.wall_construction: Traditional Khmer stilt houses (raised on wooden poles to avoid seasonal flooding) are the defining vernacular form, often made of wood, bamboo or thatch with open sides for airflow; concrete-block and stucco construction increasingly common in towns and cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural wood tones on traditional houses; brightly painted concrete shophouses in towns; gold and ornate colour on Buddhist temple architecture.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stilt houses; Buddhist wats with ornate multi-tiered roofs and gold detailing; the ancient Angkor Wat and Angkor temple complex as an unmistakable landmark; floating villages on Tonle Sap lake.

nature.vegetation: Flat rice paddies dominate the central plains; dense tropical forest surrounds the Angkor temples; sugar palm trees dotting the paddy landscape are a classic Cambodia tell.
nature.terrain: Mostly flat, low-lying central plain built around the Tonle Sap lake and the Mekong River basin; highlands and forest in the southwest (Cardamom Mountains) and northeast.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid tropical monsoon climate; dusty red laterite roads in the dry season, green flooded landscape in the rainy season.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with blue text, showing the province name in Khmer script at the top and in English at the bottom.
vehicles.plate_format: One class number, one or two Latin letters, then four digits (e.g. '2D-0888') with the province name — Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, etc.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Tuk-tuks (motorbike-drawn carriages) are a ubiquitous Cambodian tell; motorbikes vastly outnumber cars; luxury SUVs (Lexus, Toyota Land Cruiser) are disproportionately visible in Phnom Penh reflecting sharp wealth contrasts.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed — official Google coverage in cities and main highways, supplemented by Trekker imagery near temple sites.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated around Phnom Penh, Siem Reap and main highways; sparser in rural and forested areas.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Buddhist temple architecture, similar Southeast Asian tropical vegetation and motorbike-heavy traffic
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Cambodia drives on the RIGHT while Thailand drives on the LEFT; Khmer script with right-pointing hooks differs from Thai's abundance of circles; Cambodia's black-with-yellow-arrows chevron signs are the reverse of Thailand's convention.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Mekong basin geography, similar Buddhist temples, both drive on the right
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Cambodia's distinctive stone red-topped bollards and red-and-white stone road markers, plus its Khmer (rather than Lao) script, distinguish it; Cambodia is also flatter overall than mountainous Laos.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Mekong Delta geography in the south, similar rice-paddy landscape and motorbike culture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Vietnam uses Latin-script Vietnamese with heavy diacritics; Cambodia uses Khmer script; Vietnam's more densely built, narrow tube-house urban architecture differs from Cambodia's stilt houses and lower density.
